scope: Rust implementation engineering delta; no calculus, gate inventory or Writfold admission change
owner: Astra, under the user's approved architecture and implementation scope

production_dependency_additions.reason: CLI orchestration consumes the shared nominal inputs, limits and outcomes directly; forwarding re-exports or duplicate wire/core types would obscure ownership.
The control command dispatches the real stdio client; the client crate keeps all process IO out of the core crates.
The client shares the checked nominal diagnostics and limits instead of defining parallel types.
All raw peer JSON stays in wire: bounded parsing, JSON-RPC DTOs and checked conversions; the client crate itself remains serde-free.

Set normalization and algebra decisions are made by the dependency-free proved core (proofs/); the domain keeps typing, charging and origins, and re-exports the core's TraceRow and LogicalVerdict instead of defining parallel types.
The finite evaluator's per-row role and verdict are the proved core's role and classify.
weft reuse's byte-exact scope decision is the proved core's refusals; wire still never reevaluates a theory.

development_dependency_additions.reason: Report regression inputs use the real compiler rather than fabricated semantic records.
Report regressions inspect actual classifications and model-relative traces; no production wire-to-kernel edge or second evaluation.
Report fixtures compute real source digests; production source hashing remains in CLI.
CLI regression consumers decode the actual machine report; JSON semantics remain outside pure crates.

constraints: Development additions apply only to Cargo kind=dev, never normal/build dependencies.
Production wire depends on domain and the proved core only; it serializes captured results and never reevaluates proofs.
Domain, frontend and kernel remain IO-free and serde-free.
Immutable handovers and all required gate/theorem/scenario inventories remain unchanged.
Revision 3 adds no production or development dependency; set algebra extends existing crates in place.
weft-core (Aeneas shipped-kernel adoption, 2026-11-09) has no dependencies, is no_std and IO-free; domain, kernel and wire may depend on it, it depends on nothing. Registered in tools/weft-quality.
